claim_summary: The marked-root component-size family of uniform labeled Cayley forests is strictly decreasing in likelihood-ratio order as the number of specified roots grows; uniformly unrooted forest laws fail the analogous likelihood-ratio order between two and three components for every order n>=5, first at n=5.
integrity: The proof is analytic for all specified parameters. The separately supplied exact-rational verifier checks finite instances and independently enumerates both forest models. Independent external validation has not been performed.
limitations: The rooted component-size probability formula, forest enumeration, and coalescent stochastic monotonicity are classical. The claimed contribution is the cross-parameter likelihood-ratio comparison, the size-biased marked-vertex extension and an all-orders unrooted obstruction. No unrooted first-order stochastic-order failure or global unrooted classification is asserted; historical priority of the comparative formulation remains uncertain.
title: Rooting separates likelihood-ratio order from its failure in uniform Cayley forests
